title: A few backtesting mistakes that passed our initial validation
author: Kai8250
selftext:
While building a point-in-time research pipeline for a dynamic US equity universe, we found several issues that had passed our initial data-integrity checks.

The most important ones were:

Universe survivorship: data collection stopped when a symbol left the ranked universe. Entries were valid, but forward evaluation became conditional on remaining in the universe.

Backfilling missing features: bfill silently introduced values that were not available at decision time, particularly around premarket/regular-session boundaries.

Data/live contract mismatch: some fields existed in reconstructed historical data at timestamps where the live system would not have received them yet.

Non-causal ranking: selecting the top X% using the score distribution of the entire evaluation period. Fine for analysis, impossible to reproduce live.

What bothered me is that conventional integrity checks didn’t necessarily catch these. Row counts matched, calculations reproduced, timestamps looked correct, and there was no obvious label leakage.

The failure was at a different level: could the live system actually have known this value, selected this symbol, and made this decision at that exact time?

We’ve since started treating that as a separate validation layer rather than assuming a clean dataset implies a causal backtest.

For those running dynamic universes: how are you auditing historical/live information parity?
